254: static int kickpi_k7_fixed_initialize(void)
255: {
256:   size_t i;
257: 
258:   /* Stop at the first failure here, unlike rk806_initialize(): these four
259:    * rails are a parent chain (vcc12v_dcin -> vcc_sys -> vcc_2v0_pldo_s3 /
260:    * vcc_1v1_nldo_s3), so a rail whose parent is missing cannot register
261:    * either, and continuing would only repeat the same failure further down.
262:    */
263: 
264:   for (i = 0; i < nitems(g_kickpi_k7_fixed_rails); i++)
265:     {
266:       if (regulator_register(&g_kickpi_k7_fixed_rails[i],
267:                              &g_kickpi_k7_fixed_ops, NULL) == NULL)
268:         {
269:           syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: failed to register fixed rail %s\n",
270:                  g_kickpi_k7_fixed_rails[i].name);
271:           return -ENODEV;
272:         }
273: 
274:       syslog(LOG_INFO, "Registered fixed regulator %s (%u uV)\n",
275:              g_kickpi_k7_fixed_rails[i].name,
276:              g_kickpi_k7_fixed_rails[i].min_uv);
277:     }
278: 
279:   return OK;
280: }

284: /****************************************************************************
285:  * Public Functions
286:  ****************************************************************************/

288: /****************************************************************************
289:  * Name: kickpi_k7_regulator_initialize
290:  *
291:  * Description:
292:  *   Initialize the on-board RK806 PMIC, which is wired to the I2C1 bus
293:  *   (I2C1 M0 signal group).  This function is guarded by
294:  *   CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_REGULATOR (which itself requires CONFIG_REGULATOR_RK806
295:  *   and CONFIG_RK3576_I2C).
296:  *
297:  *   See the "Notes on the RK806 regulator tree" block above: any parent
298:  *   ("supply") regulator for the RK806 outputs must be registered here,
299:  *   before rk806_initialize() is called.
300:  *
301:  * Returned Value:
302:  *   Zero (OK) on success, or a negated errno on failure.
303:  *
304:  ****************************************************************************/
305: 
306: int kickpi_k7_regulator_initialize(void)
307: {
308: #ifndef CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_REGULATOR
309:   return -ENODEV;
310: #else
311:   FAR struct gpio_dev_s *scl;
312:   FAR struct gpio_dev_s *sda;
313:   FAR struct i2c_master_s *i2c1;
314:   int ret;
315: 
316:   /* Register the fixed input rails first: rk806_initialize() resolves each
317:    * PMIC output's parent through regulator_get(), and the parent must
318:    * already be on the regulator list.
319:    */
320: 
321:   ret = kickpi_k7_fixed_initialize();
322:   if (ret < 0)
323:     {
324:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to init fixed regulators\n");
325:       return ret;
326:     }
327: 
328:   /* Mux the I2C1 signal group.  The handles are deliberately not put():
329:    * once muxed, the pads belong to the I2C controller for as long as it
330:    * runs.
331:    */
332: 
333:   ret = rk3576_gpio_get(KICKPI_K7_I2C1_SCL_PIN, &scl);
334:   if (ret < 0)
335:     {
336:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: failed to claim I2C1 SCL (GPIO0_B2): %d\n", ret);
337:       return ret;
338:     }
339: 
340:   rk3576_gpio_set_af(scl, KICKPI_K7_I2C1_AF);
341: 
342:   ret = rk3576_gpio_get(KICKPI_K7_I2C1_SDA_PIN, &sda);
343:   if (ret < 0)
344:     {
345:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: failed to claim I2C1 SDA (GPIO0_B3): %d\n", ret);
346:       return ret;
347:     }
348: 
349:   rk3576_gpio_set_af(sda, KICKPI_K7_I2C1_AF);
350: 
351:   i2c1 = rk3576_i2c_initialize(1);
352:   if (i2c1 == NULL)
353:     {
354:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "Failed to init I2C1\n");
355:       return -EIO;
356:     }
357: 
358:   ret = rk806_initialize(i2c1, g_kickpi_k7_rk806_cfg, RK806_NUM_OUTPUTS);
359:   if (ret < 0)
360:     {
361:       /* Not fatal: rk806_initialize() reports a failure for a single rail
362:        * while the others stay registered, so the tree is partial rather than
363:        * absent (see the contract in rk806.h).
364:        */
365: 
366:       syslog(LOG_ERR, "RK806: rail tree incomplete (%d), some rails are up\n",
367:              ret);
368:       return ret;
369:     }
370: 
371:   return OK;
372: #endif

我核对了代码、DTS 和 regulator 框架，结论是：**这条交叉审查意见在机制上成立，DTS 依据也属实，而且它把范围说小了**，实际不一致的轨有 17 条，不是 5 条。唯一的补充是：当前树里还没有任何消费者，所以这是“一旦有人用就会踩”的潜在缺陷，不是现在就一定会挂。

## 逐条核实

| 审查意见 | 核实结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 宏里 `always_on` 隐式为 false | 属实。[kickpi_k7_regulator.c:189](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_regulator.c#L189>) 的宏只给 `.boot_on = true`；表是 static 数组，未写出的字段为 0 |
| `boot_on` 只负责注册时上电 | 属实。[regulator.c:1060](<nuttx/drivers/power/supply/regulator.c#L1060>) 在注册时直接调 `_regulator_do_enable()`，**不经过 `regulator_enable()`，也不增加 `use_count`** |
| 框架在 `use_count` 1→0 时调 disable | 属实。[regulator.c:811](<nuttx/drivers/power/supply/regulator.c#L811>)：`use_count == 1 && !always_on` 就调 `_regulator_do_disable()` |
| 会真的切断供电 | 属实。这 17 条 READBACK 轨走 `g_rk806_ops`（[rk806.c:553](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/drivers/drivers/rk806/rk806.c#L553>)），`rk806_disable()`（[rk806.c:472](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/drivers/drivers/rk806/rk806.c#L472>)）会把对应的 POWER_EN 状态位清 0，不是空操作 |
| K7 原始 DTS 对这些轨标了 `regulator-always-on` | 属实。见 `out/k7dtb` 里解出的 K7 DTB：DCDC_REG1(vdd_cpu_big_s0) 5239、REG3(vdd_cpu_lit_s0) 5269、REG4(vcc_3v3_s3) 5285、REG7(vdd_logic_s0) 5325、REG8(vcc_1v8_s3) 5339 全部带 `regulator-always-on` |
| AMP 部署下更不能断 | 有独立证据：`tools/amp/linux/rk3576-kickpi-k7-amp.dtsi` 专门给 `vdd_cpu_lit_s0`、`vdd_logic_s0` 重新加回 `regulator-always-on`（[rk3576-kickpi-k7-amp.dtsi:100](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/tools/amp/linux/rk3576-kickpi-k7-amp.dtsi#L100>)），因为 openvela 就跑在 A53 上 |

## 审查意见说小了的地方

我按 DTS 逐轨统计了一遍：

- **19/21 条轨在 K7 DTS 里是 `regulator-always-on`**，只有 `vdd_npu_s0` 和 `vdd_gpu_s0` 是单纯的 `regulator-boot-on`（DCDC_REG2/DCDC_REG5）。
- 而 NuttX 这边只有两条 DDR 轨设了 `always_on`，也就是说**有 17 条轨与 DTS 不符**，不止审查点名的 5 条。
- 尤其值得注意的是 **`vdd_ddr_s0`（DCDC_REG10，DRAM 轨）**：它是 READBACK 而不是 UNKNOWN，所以落在普通宏里，同样只 `boot_on`。一次 enable/disable 就能关掉 DRAM 供电，后果和关 CPU 轨一样致命。文件里那句“Only the DDR rails are always-on”（[kickpi_k7_regulator.c:184](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_regulator.c#L184>)）因此本身也不准确——DDR 三轨里只有两轨是 `always_on`。

## 影响面：潜在缺陷，但不必推翻“P1”

- 全仓库（apps + nuttx）搜不到任何对板级轨的 `regulator_enable/disable` 调用；`drivertest_regulator` 用的是自己注册的 fake 轨，不碰板级轨。
- 只有 `configs/dev` 打开了 `CONFIG_KICKPI_K7_REGULATOR`（[defconfig:240](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/configs/dev/defconfig#L240>)），camera/hdmi/display 等配置里这个驱动根本没编进去，所以当前出货固件不会因此挂。
- 但文件注释自己写着“future consumer drivers (SDIO voltage switching, peripheral power sequencing) can enable and disable them on demand”（[kickpi_k7_regulator.c:184](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_regulator.c#L184>)）——第一个这样的消费者落地时，就会写 POWER_EN=0。
- 还有一个值得写进审查回复的事实：**`always_on=n` 并没换来电量收益**。注册时 `boot_on=true` 已经把所有 21 条轨都打开了；`always_on` 的唯一作用是“以后能不能关”。所以现状不是“省电 vs 安全”的取舍，而是“保留一个关电闸的把手 vs 不保留”。
- 补充一个机制细节：`_regulator_do_disable()` 还会连带 `regulator_disable()` 父轨（[regulator.c:145](<nuttx/drivers/power/supply/regulator.c#L145>)），不过父轨是 fixed 且 `always_on`，这条链上不会二次伤害。

“把 `always_on` 做成可选宏属性”技术上完全可行，而且改动很小。我更推荐**再加一个宏**（和已有的 `KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_UNKNOWN` 风格一致），比变参 `__VA_ARGS__` 更好读、也不依赖空参数时尾逗号的编译器扩展：

```c
#define KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_AO(_name, _supply, _min, _max)          \
  {                                                                  \
    .name = _name, .supply = _supply, .min_uv = _min, .max_uv = _max,\
    .voltage_source = RK806_VOLTAGE_READBACK, .boot_on = true,       \
    .always_on = true                                                \
  }
```

按 DTS 精确对齐的话，除 `vdd_npu_s0`、`vdd_gpu_s0` 外全部用 AO 宏；只求最小改动的话，至少要把审查点名的 5 条加上 `vdd_ddr_s0` 改掉。同时必须改掉 [kickpi_k7_regulator.c:184](<contest2026_062_PharosTech/boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_regulator.c#L184>) 那段注释，以及 1722bc2 提交里“remaining rails keep always_on=n so future consumers can power them down”的说法——否则注释和代码会继续各说各话。

**总评**：审查意见没有事实错误，机制、框架行为、DTS 依据我都复核通过；可以按 P1 接受（它会在消费者落地的第一天变成真故障），只需在回复里把范围从“5 条关键轨”更正为“17 条与 DTS 不符，其中 6 条一旦被关会立刻宕机”。需要的话我可以直接把这个改动做出来并跑一遍 `dev` 配置的编译验证。

 * part is written once here.
 */

#define KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_FIELDS(_name, _supply, _min, _max, _vs) \
  .name = _name, .supply = _supply, .min_uv = _min, .max_uv = _max,  \
  .voltage_source = _vs, .boot_on = true

/* Controllable READBACK rail: boot-on only in the board DTS. */

#define KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL(_name, _supply, _min, _max)             \
  {                                                                  \
    KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_FIELDS(_name, _supply, _min, _max,          \
                                RK806_VOLTAGE_READBACK)              \
  }

/* Always-on READBACK rail: the board DTS marks it regulator-always-on, so it
 * is enabled at registration and regulator_disable() never reaches the PMIC.
 */

#define KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_AO(_name, _supply, _min, _max)          \
  {                                                                  \
    KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_FIELDS(_name, _supply, _min, _max,          \
                                RK806_VOLTAGE_READBACK),             \
    .always_on = true                                                \
  }

/* Read-only UNKNOWN rail (external feedback, no usable VSEL register).  Also
 * always-on: enable/disable have no callback to reach, but saying so keeps the
 * descriptor consistent with the board DTS.
 */

#define KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_UNKNOWN(_name, _supply)                 \
  {                                                                  \
    KICKPI_K7_RK806_RAIL_FIELDS(_name, _supply, 0, 0,                \
                                RK806_VOLTAGE_UNKNOWN),              \
    .always_on = true                                                \
  }
